where: Posts #91, #98–#100 and the final replies of agents 2, 3, and 4.
answer_reason: The team unanimously states that the exact infimum is 1/9 and that both proof halves are complete.

review.claimed: The infimum is 1/9: every c>1/9 has a finite triangle-free universal homomorphism target, while every c<1/9 fails.

decisive_steps.checked: Checked the degree accounting: after discarding bad clusters, d_R(i)m >= (c-d-2ε-3√ε)n >= qn, and each vertex has at least qn neighbors in its profile clusters. Checked all short-cycle embeddings. For a common reduced neighbor, regularity provides a vertex adjacent to both large neighbor subsets; when the subsets occupy the same cluster, triangle-freeness makes them disjoint. Avoiding the finitely many prescribed vertices ensures genuine cycles. The equitable regularity lemma invoked is standard and applies as stated.

decisive_steps.step: Nine-block packing establishes bounded coloring of W(G) for c>1/9 (agent_1 final, §2.2; channel #75–#77).
decisive_steps.checked: Verified that equal colors (profile, set of neighbor profiles) along x-b-c-y provide matching neighbors b' and c'. The resulting three odd walks force all three profiles to have size at least 2qk. Actual edges give pairwise disjoint profiles and reduced-neighborhood sets; the three length-two walks give all cross anticompleteness. Thus the six sets are genuinely pairwise disjoint and have total size at least 9qk>k.

decisive_steps.step: A bounded coloring of W(G) yields one finite triangle-free target (agent_1 final, §1).
decisive_steps.checked: Checked the explicit target on pairs (i,S). Its edge conditions exclude triangles, and the proposed map preserves every edge because adjacent vertices have disjoint neighbor-color sets. The color bound depends only on c; smaller graph orders can be incorporated by increasing the same bound.

decisive_steps.step: Elementary shift graphs supply arbitrarily high chromatic number and near-half supports disjoint along odd walks of length one or three (agent_1 final, §§3.1–3.2).
decisive_steps.checked: Verified the extension-color-set recursion down to S_1(m)=K_m. Checked cancellation of alternating scores on edges and its telescoping along odd walks. These identities prove both support disjointness and absence of closed odd walks of length at most five for k>5. The binomial support formula and central-binomial estimate correctly give p_k→1/2.

decisive_steps.step: Cyclic three-layer construction proves failure below 1/9 (agent_1 final, §3.3).
decisive_steps.checked: Checked the complete classification of short odd cycles by their number of sparse edges. One sparse edge cannot return to its starting layer; three sparse edges with two dense edges contradict support disjointness; all-sparse short odd cycles project to forbidden closed walks. Equal endpoint image triples on a base edge would force a triangle in the target, giving the required coloring contradiction. The minimum-degree ratio tends to p_k/[3(1+p_k)]→1/9.

decisive_steps.step: Executable checks accompanying the final proof.
decisive_steps.checked: Read and reran workspace/agent1_answer_code.py, removing only its self-copy command, and workspace/agent4_lift_standalone.py, removing only its output-file write. Both passed. Reproduced the 840-vertex, 12,675-edge graph with minimum degree 16 and traces A^3=A^5=0; reproduced 28,263 reduced graphs and 960 admissible six-block triples; and reproduced the independent 936-vertex construction with minimum degree 28 and both traces zero. The integer computations have no overflow at these sizes. These are supplementary checks; the infinite statements have written proofs.

review.failing_step: The hardest step is the upper bound's derivation of six pairwise-disjoint reduced-graph blocks from an equal-colored length-three walk; it holds.
review.reason: Both halves are complete and force the same value 1/9. The early objection to the five-block argument is resolved by the final neighbor-profile refinement and length-two-walk constraints, not merely by agreement. Speculative literature recollections and Kneser/Borsuk constructions are not used in the final proof, and no substantive final gap remains.

contract.form: A complete answer must give a single exact real number in [0,1] equal to the infimum of the values c having the stated property, and justify that it is the infimum. It need not determine whether the property holds at the infimum itself.
contract.not_enough: Bounds or a range without an exact value, an approximation alone, an assertion that the value is unknown or undetermined, a conjecture-conditional value, or verification of the property only for selected values of c would not settle the question.

definite_reason: It gives a single exact real number in [0,1] as the requested infimum; if true, it would settle the question.
